prediction.likelyOutcome: Covenant has a modestly better-than-even shot at persuading a jury that the lease never commenced — the Exhibit G outer-date arithmetic (April 23, 2020) combined with Empower's April 13, 2020 permit application and eighteen months of self-interested delay is a strong, jury-friendly story, and the court's ambiguity finding opens the door to the favorable broker email and LOI. Most likely result is a defense verdict on Empower's counterclaim and return of the $96,291.09 deposit, with fees a toss-up under the DJA. The risk, though small in probability, is severe in magnitude: a jury finding Section 3(c) to be a mere covenant exposes Covenant to twelve years of rent on a 19,331 sq ft building, an amount this record does not permit me to quantify.

outcome.description: After a four-day jury trial the jury found Section 3(c) was a condition precedent that Empower failed to satisfy; the trial court rendered judgment declaring the lease abrogated and ordered Empower to pay Covenant $96,291.09 in damages (the deposit), $611,491.45 in attorney's fees, and $135,000 in conditional appellate fees. The court of appeals held Section 3(c) is a covenant, not a condition precedent, reversed the entire judgment, rendered take-nothing on the condition-precedent declarations, and remanded the remaining declarations, the damages and fee awards, and Empower's breach-of-contract counterclaim.
